  2. In die Navigation in mkdocs.yml unter nav: aufnehmen (deutscher Titel), den englischen Titel unter nav_translations ergänzen und in funktionen/index.md und funktionen/index.en.md verlinken.

  3. Screenshot in scripts/docs-screenshots/capture.mjs in der Liste SHOTS ergänzen und einbinden:

    ![Spendenübersicht](../assets/screenshots/donations.png){ .screenshot }

    Beide Sprachfassungen verweisen auf dieselbe donations.png; englische Seiten bekommen automatisch donations.en.png. Das Skript findet Knöpfe über ihre Beschriftung in den Übersetzungsdateien der App – nutze t('…') mit dem i18n-Schlüssel statt fester Texte.

  4. Betroffene Seiten anpassen: Rollen, Übersicht, Datenschutz, Daten exportieren.

  5. Braucht das Update Handarbeit der Nutzer? Dann Eintrag in den Versionshinweisen in beiden Sprachen nach der Vorlage docs/templates/migration-guide.md und Label breaking-change am PR.

docs.title: Lokal ausprobieren
docs.text:
pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
npm run docs:serve        # Vorschau auf http://127.0.0.1:8000 (Englisch unter /en/)
npm run docs:build        # wie in CI: Coverage-Prüfung + strenger Build
npm run docs:screenshots  # alle Screenshots neu erzeugen (braucht Go und Node)

docs:screenshots startet ein eigenes Backend und Frontend auf den Ports 3101 und 5273 mit einer Wegwerf-Datenbank, richtet sie mit Beispieldaten ein und fotografiert alle Seiten. Deine eigene Installation bleibt unberührt. Das passiert einmal je Sprache. Damit sich Screenshots nur ändern, wenn sich die Oberfläche ändert, ist die Uhr im Browser eingefroren, Animationen sind abgeschaltet, zufällige IDs und Zeitstempel in Tabellen werden durch feste Werte ersetzt, und eine Datei wird nur überschrieben, wenn sich Pixel über die Farbtoleranz für Kantenglättung hinaus geändert haben. DOCS_LANGUAGES=en erzeugt nur eine Sprache.

docs.title: Schreibstil
docs.text:
• Deutsch: Du-Form, kurze Sätze, wie in der App. Englisch: einfach, freundlich, direkte Anrede.
  • Für Ehrenamtliche ohne IT-Kenntnisse schreiben: Was muss ich klicken, was passiert dann?
  • Bezeichnungen von Knöpfen und Menüs fett und genau so, wie sie in der App in der jeweiligen Sprache stehen.
  • Ehrlich sein: Was (noch) nicht geht, steht in einem Hinweis-Kasten.
  • Keine echten Personendaten in Beispielen und Screenshots.

docs.title: Zusammenarbeit
docs.text:
Mit der Zusammenarbeit arbeiten mehrere Personen aus dem Vorstand mit denselben Vereinsdaten – jede auf ihrem eigenen Computer, auch wenn ihr nicht im selben Netzwerk seid.

Noch in Entwicklung

Die Zusammenarbeit ist neu. Probiere sie aus, aber verlasse dich für echte Bankdaten erst darauf, wenn Version 1.0 erschienen ist und das Verfahren von Fachleuten für Kryptografie geprüft wurde.

docs.title: So funktioniert es
docs.text:
Laptop Vorstand           PC Kassierer            Laptop Übungsleiterin
 ┌──────────────┐          ┌──────────────┐          ┌──────────────┐
 │ eigene Daten │          │ eigene Daten │          │ eigene Daten │
 └──────┬───────┘          └──────┬───────┘          └──────┬───────┘
        │   verschlüsselte, unterschriebene Änderungen      │
        └───────────────►  gemeinsamer Ordner  ◄────────────┘
                (Nextcloud, OneDrive, Dropbox, Google Drive, Netzlaufwerk)
  • Jedes Gerät hat seine eigene Datenbank. Du arbeitest immer lokal und schnell, auch ohne Internet.
  • Änderungen werden ausgetauscht, nicht die Datenbank. Jede Änderung wird verschlüsselt, vom Gerät unterschrieben und als Datei im gemeinsamen Ordner abgelegt. Die anderen Geräte holen sie sich von dort.
  • Der Ordner sieht nur verschlüsselte Daten. Weder euer Cloud-Anbieter noch jemand, der den Ordner öffnet, kann Mitglieder- oder Bankdaten lesen.
  • Rechte sind technisch abgesichert. Ein Gerät mit der Rolle Übungsleiter bekommt den Schlüssel für Bankdaten gar nicht – es kann sie also auch nicht lesen, wenn jemand die Dateien direkt öffnet.
  • Kein Server nötig. Ihr nutzt einen Ordner, den der Verein schon hat.

docs.title: Was ihr braucht
docs.text:
1. Einen gemeinsamen Ordner, auf den alle Beteiligten Schreibzugriff haben und der auf ihren Computern synchronisiert wird – über das Sync-Programm von Nextcloud, OneDrive, Dropbox oder Google Drive. Ein Netzlaufwerk geht auch, wenn alle es erreichen (z. B. per VPN).
  2. Open ClubManager auf jedem Gerät.
  3. Eine Person aus dem Vorstand, die den Verein einrichtet und die anderen einlädt.

docs.title: Der Sync-Status
docs.text:
Oben in der Kopfzeile zeigt ein Symbol den Stand der Zusammenarbeit:

Anzeige Bedeutung Alles synchronisiert Deine Änderungen sind im Ordner, die der anderen sind da. Wird synchronisiert … Open ClubManager tauscht gerade Änderungen aus (automatisch alle 30 Sekunden). Speicherort nicht erreichbar Der Ordner ist gerade nicht da (z. B. offline). Du kannst normal weiterarbeiten; deine Änderungen warten und werden später übertragen. Bitte ansehen Es gibt Klärungsbedarf, Beitrittsanfragen oder ein Problem. Warte auf Bestätigung Du hast den Beitritt angefragt, der Vorstand muss noch zustimmen.

Mit Jetzt synchronisieren stößt du den Austausch sofort an.

Wie schnell kommen Änderungen an?

Open ClubManager selbst schaut alle 30 Sekunden nach. Wie schnell eine Änderung im Ordner der anderen ankommt, hängt aber vom Sync-Programm eures Cloud-Anbieters ab – meist Sekunden bis wenige Minuten.

docs.title: Gleichzeitige Änderungen
docs.text:
Ändern zwei Personen gleichzeitig unterschiedliche Felder desselben Mitglieds (z. B. die eine die Adresse, der andere die IBAN), bleiben beide Änderungen erhalten. Ändern beide dasselbe Feld, gewinnt die zeitlich spätere Änderung.

Werte, die eindeutig sein müssen – Mitgliedsnummern, E-Mail-Adressen, Namen von Gruppen und Abteilungen – können dabei doppelt vergeben werden. Das wird unter Klärungsbedarf angezeigt.

docs.title: Seiten in diesem Abschnitt
docs.text:
• Verein einrichten
  • Einem Verein beitreten
  • Personen & Geräte verwalten
  • Klärungsbedarf
  • Notfallschlüssel

docs.title: Einem Verein beitreten
docs.text: Du wurdest eingeladen und hast einen Einladungscode bekommen? So trittst du bei.

docs.title: Vorher
docs.text:
• Installiere Open ClubManager und lege bei der Ersteinrichtung dein Konto an (Auswahl: „Gemeinsam mit anderen – ich habe eine Einladung“).
  • Nimm die Ordnerfreigabe an, die du von deinem Verein bekommen hast (Nextcloud, OneDrive, Dropbox, Google Drive …), und sorge dafür, dass der Ordner auf deinem Computer synchronisiert wird.

docs.title: 1. Einladungscode
docs.text: Gib den 24-stelligen Code ein oder füge ihn ein. Bindestriche, Leerzeichen und Groß-/Kleinschreibung sind egal. Der Code ist 7 Tage gültig und funktioniert nur einmal.

docs.title: 2. Speicherort
docs.text:
Wähle den freigegebenen Ordner. Open ClubManager zeigt an, welcher Verein darin liegt.

Vorhandene Daten auf diesem Gerät

Gibt es auf deinem Gerät schon Vereinsdaten, werden sie durch die Daten des Vereins ersetzt. Vorher wird neben der Datenbank automatisch eine Sicherung gespeichert. Du musst dem ausdrücklich zustimmen.

docs.title: 3. Dein Name
docs.text: Dein Name und der Name dieses Geräts, damit die anderen dich erkennen. Dazu dein Passwort, das den Schlüssel dieses Geräts schützt.

docs.title: 4. Sicherheitscode
docs.text:
Du siehst einen 6-stelligen Sicherheitscode. Nenne ihn der Person, die dich eingeladen hat – am besten am Telefon. Erst wenn sie ihn bestätigt, bekommst du Zugriff.

Du kannst Open ClubManager solange schließen. Sobald du bestätigt bist, siehst du „Willkommen! Du bist jetzt dabei“ und deine Rolle.

Falscher Code oder falscher Ordner? Mit Beitritt abbrechen ziehst du deine Anfrage zurück – auf diesem Bildschirm oder unter Zusammenarbeit. Danach kannst du es sofort noch einmal versuchen.

Warum ein Sicherheitscode?

Der Code stellt sicher, dass wirklich du die Einladung benutzt hast und nicht jemand, der die Einladungs-E-Mail abgefangen hat.

docs.title: Wenn es nicht klappt
docs.text: Meldung Was tun „Diesen Einladungscode kennen wir nicht“ Code prüfen oder neue Einladung anfordern. Wurde die Einladung gerade erst erstellt, warten, bis das Sync-Programm den Ordner abgeglichen hat, und erneut versuchen „In diesem Ordner ist kein Verein“ Prüfen, ob du die Freigabe angenommen hast und dein Sync-Programm läuft „Die Einladung ist abgelaufen / wurde schon verwendet“ Neue Einladung anfordern „Dieses Gerät wurde nicht in den Verein aufgenommen“ Der Vorstand hat die Anfrage abgelehnt. An ihn wenden; mit „Erneut versuchen“ kannst du neu beitreten

docs.title: Verein für Zusammenarbeit einrichten
docs.text:
Das macht eine Person aus dem Vorstand, einmalig. Sie bekommt dabei die Rolle Vorstand und kann danach die anderen einladen.

Starte über Zusammenarbeit → Zusammenarbeit einschalten (oder bei der Ersteinrichtung mit „Gemeinsam mit anderen – neuen Verein einrichten“).

docs.title: 1. Speicherort
docs.text:
Wähle den gemeinsamen Ordner. Open ClubManager zeigt Ordner von Nextcloud, OneDrive, Dropbox und Google Drive an, die es auf deinem Computer findet. Mit Anderen Ordner angeben … gibst du einen eigenen Pfad oder ein Netzlaufwerk an (z. B. \\vereinsserver\vorstand oder /Volumes/Verein).

Open ClubManager prüft den Ordner:

  • wird synchronisiert – passt
  • Netzlaufwerk – passt, wenn alle darauf zugreifen können
  • scheint nicht synchronisiert zu werden – andere können dann nicht auf die Daten zugreifen
  • nicht beschreibbar oder existiert nicht – Pfad und Berechtigung prüfen

Im Ordner wird ein Unterordner „Open ClubManager – Vereinsname“ angelegt.

docs.title: 2. Verein und du
docs.text:
• Vereinsname
  • Dein Name – so sehen dich die anderen
  • Name dieses Geräts – z. B. „Laptop“ oder „Büro-PC“
  • Dein Passwort – das Passwort, mit dem du dich in Open ClubManager anmeldest. Es schützt den Schlüssel dieses Geräts.

Die Daten, die schon auf diesem Gerät sind, werden zum Startstand des Vereins.

docs.title: 3. Notfallschlüssel
docs.text:
Open ClubManager erzeugt einen Notfallschlüssel. Ohne ihn kommt niemand mehr an die Vereinsdaten, wenn alle Vorstandsgeräte verloren gehen.

  • Drucke ihn aus oder speichere ihn als Datei an einem sicheren Ort – nicht im gemeinsamen Ordner.
  • Zur Kontrolle tippst du die letzten 4 Zeichen der Zeile „check:“ ab.
  • Open ClubManager speichert den Schlüssel danach nicht.

Mehr dazu unter Notfallschlüssel.

docs.title: 4. Fertig
docs.text: Als Nächstes lädst du die anderen ein.

docs.title: Klärungsbedarf
docs.text: Weil jedes Gerät auch offline arbeitet, können zwei Personen gleichzeitig denselben eindeutigen Wert vergeben – zum Beispiel beide die Mitgliedsnummer 1042 für zwei verschiedene neue Mitglieder. Open ClubManager erkennt das und zeigt es unter Zusammenarbeit → Klärungsbedarf an (auch über den Sync-Status „Bitte ansehen“).

docs.title: Was kann doppelt sein?
docs.text:
• Mitgliedsnummern
  • E-Mail-Adressen von Mitgliedern
  • Namen von Gruppen, Rollen und Abteilungen

docs.title: So löst du es
docs.text:
Für jeden Fall zeigt Open ClubManager, welcher Eintrag den Wert behält und welcher geändert werden muss. Die Regel: Den Wert behält, wer ihn zuerst vergeben hat.

Fall Lösung Mitgliedsnummer doppelt Nächste freie Nummer vergeben oder Nummer selbst wählen E-Mail-Adresse doppelt eine neue E-Mail-Adresse eintragen Name doppelt einen neuen Namen eintragen

Klicke auf Übernehmen. Die Änderung wird an alle verteilt, und der Eintrag verschwindet aus der Liste.

Klären kann das jeder, der für den betroffenen Bereich Schreibrecht hat. Wer nur lesen darf, sieht den Hinweis, kann aber nichts ändern.

docs.title: Notfallschlüssel
docs.text: Der Notfallschlüssel wird beim Einrichten des Vereins einmalig erzeugt. Mit ihm kommt ihr wieder an eure Vereinsdaten und die Verwaltung, wenn kein Gerät mit der Rolle Vorstand mehr verfügbar ist – zum Beispiel, weil der einzige Vorstandslaptop gestohlen wurde.

docs.title: Aufbewahren
docs.text:
• Bewahre ihn auf wie einen Tresorschlüssel: ausgedruckt im Vereinsordner, im Bankschließfach, beim Vorsitzenden zu Hause.
  • Nicht im gemeinsamen Cloud-Ordner speichern – wer Ordner und Notfallschlüssel hat, hat vollen Zugriff.
  • Niemand sonst kann ihn wiederherstellen – auch nicht die Entwickler von Open ClubManager.

docs.title: Verwenden
docs.text:
Nur verwenden, wenn wirklich kein Vorstandsgerät mehr da ist.

  1. Installiere Open ClubManager auf einem Gerät und starte die Einrichtung mit Notfallschlüssel verwenden (oder unter Zusammenarbeit → Notfall).
  2. Füge den ganzen Text des Notfallschlüssels ein oder tippe ihn ab. Wichtig sind die Zeilen club-id, root-sign-key, root-age-key und check.
  3. Klicke auf Verein wiederherstellen.

Dieses Gerät ist danach ein Vorstandsgerät. Entferne als Nächstes unter Personen & Geräte alle Geräte, die verloren gegangen sind.

Der Notfallschlüssel bleibt gültig – bewahre ihn wieder sicher auf.

docs.title: Häufige Fehler
docs.text: Meldung Bedeutung „Der Notfallschlüssel ist unvollständig oder enthält einen Tippfehler“ Text prüfen, besonders die Zeile check „Dieser Notfallschlüssel gehört zu einem anderen Verein“ falscher Schlüssel oder falscher Ordner

docs.title: Personen & Geräte
docs.text: Unter Zusammenarbeit findest du die Reiter Übersicht, Personen & Geräte, Einladungen, Rollen und Notfall. Einladen, Rollen ändern und Geräte entfernen darf nur der Vorstand.

docs.title: Person einladen
docs.text:
1. Wer und welche Rolle: Name der Person und ihre Rolle (Vorstand, Kassierer, Schriftführer, Übungsleiter, Gerätewart). Open ClubManager zeigt, was die Rolle darf.
  2. Zugang zum Ordner: Gib der Person bei eurem Cloud-Anbieter Schreibzugriff auf den gemeinsamen Ordner. Das geht nicht über Open ClubManager – du bekommst aber eine Schritt-für-Schritt-Anleitung für Nextcloud, OneDrive, Dropbox oder Google Drive.
  3. Einladungscode: Schicke der Person den Code, z. B. per E-Mail oder Messenger. Mit E-Mail-Text anzeigen bekommst du einen fertigen Text zum Kopieren.

Der Code ist 7 Tage gültig und funktioniert einmal. Offene Einladungen siehst du im Reiter Einladungen und kannst sie dort zurückziehen.

docs.title: Beitrittsanfrage bestätigen
docs.text:
Wenn die eingeladene Person beitritt, erscheint bei dir eine Beitrittsanfrage.

  1. Ruf die Person an und frag nach dem Sicherheitscode, den sie auf ihrem Bildschirm sieht.
  2. Gib ihn ein und klicke auf Zugriff geben.

Stimmt der Code nicht, lehne die Anfrage ab – dann hat jemand anderes die Einladung benutzt. Nach drei falschen Codes wird die Anfrage automatisch abgelehnt.

docs.title: Rollen
docs.text:
Die fünf Rollen sind fest vorgegeben:

Rolle Darf Vorstand alles sehen und bearbeiten, andere einladen Kassierer Bankdaten und Finanzen bearbeiten, Mitglieder und Kontakte sehen Schriftführer Mitglieder und Kontaktdaten pflegen Übungsleiter Mitgliederliste und Inventar sehen Gerätewart Inventar bearbeiten, Mitgliederliste sehen

Die vollständige Tabelle steht unter Benutzer & Rollen.

docs.title: Rolle ändern
docs.text: Unter Personen & Geräte → Rolle ändern. Bekommt jemand weniger Rechte, sieht er neue Daten aus den entzogenen Bereichen ab sofort nicht mehr. Was er bereits gesehen hat, bleibt auf seinem Gerät.

docs.title: Gerät entfernen
docs.text:
Wenn ein Gerät verloren geht, gestohlen wird oder jemand aus dem Amt ausscheidet: Personen & Geräte → Gerät entfernen und den Grund wählen.

Danach gilt:

  • Das Gerät erhält keine neuen Daten mehr.
  • Änderungen, die es ab jetzt macht, werden von allen ignoriert.
  • Was bereits auf dem Gerät gespeichert ist, kann nicht gelöscht werden.

Verlust oder Diebstahl: Datenpanne melden

Geht ein Gerät mit Mitgliederdaten verloren, kann das eine Datenpanne sein, die innerhalb von 72 Stunden der Datenschutzaufsichtsbehörde gemeldet werden muss (Art. 33 DSGVO). Festplattenverschlüsselung senkt das Risiko erheblich.

Dein eigenes Gerät kannst du nicht entfernen. Es muss immer mindestens ein Gerät mit der Rolle Vorstand geben.

docs.title: Data protection
docs.text:
Clubs process personal data, often including bank details and data about children. Open ClubManager helps you comply with the GDPR. The club remains responsible, though.

Not legal advice

This page explains how Open ClubManager handles data and which features help you. It is not legal advice. Many sports federations and umbrella organisations provide templates for privacy notices and records of processing activities.

docs.title: Where is the data stored?
docs.text:
Mode Where Who has access Only on this device in the database file on your computer whoever has access to your computer and your user account Collaboration on every participating device, plus encrypted in the shared folder the invited devices, each only the areas of its role

Open ClubManager sends no data to the developers or to analytics or advertising services. There is no telemetry.

docs.title: Cloud folders in collaboration
docs.text: In the shared folder, member and bank data is only stored encrypted. The cloud provider does see technical metadata, though: file names, file sizes, timestamps, device names, the access list and join requests. Check whether you need a data processing agreement with the provider; with a club-owned Nextcloud this is usually not necessary.

docs.title: Protection on the device
docs.text:
The database on the device is not additionally encrypted. Protect it by:

  • turning on disk encryption (BitLocker, FileVault, LUKS)
  • locking your computer with a password
  • protecting backups just like the database
  • deleting exports (Excel, CSV, PDF) after use

docs.title: GDPR features
docs.text: Obligation Feature in Open ClubManager Right of access (Art. 15) data export as PDF per member Data portability (Art. 20) data export as JSON Rectification (Art. 16) edit member Erasure (Art. 17) delete member Access restriction user roles and device roles Accountability history of all changes Data breach (Art. 33) remove device with a note on the 72-hour deadline Police clearance certificates (§ 72a SGB VIII, Germany) store inspection date only

docs.title: Collaboration considerations
docs.text: Data a device has already received cannot be "taken back", neither by changing its role nor by removing the device. This is true for any software. So only invite people who really need the data for their position, and choose the role with the fewest permissions necessary.

docs.title: Open ClubManager
docs.text:
Free club management software for your computer. Members, fees, events, attendance and inventory: no subscription, no cloud account, no IT department needed.

Still in development

Version 1.0 of Open ClubManager has not been released yet. Try out everything you like, but don't store real bank details in it until the first stable release is out.

docs.title: Who is Open ClubManager for?
docs.text: Small and medium-sized clubs and associations that are run today with spreadsheets, word-processor templates and a lot of memory work: sports clubs, music societies, booster clubs, cultural associations. It is made for the volunteers who do the work: the board, the treasurer, the secretary, the coaches.

docs.title: What Open ClubManager is
docs.text:
• A program for your computer (Windows, macOS, Linux). You install it like any other program.
  • Free and open source, permanently, with no member limit.
  • Local: your data is stored in a file on your computer. Nobody else has access to it.
  • Works offline: you only need the internet if you work together with others.
  • Usable as a team: several board members can work together. The data is exchanged in encrypted form through a folder your club already has (Nextcloud, OneDrive, Dropbox, Google Drive, a network drive). See Collaboration.

docs.title: What Open ClubManager is not
docs.text:
• Not a web application. There is no website to log in to and no mobile app. Open ClubManager only runs as an installed program.
  • Not a member portal. Members don't log in or maintain their own data.
  • Not tax accounting. The cash book helps with fees, income and expenses, but it does not replace double-entry bookkeeping or your tax advisor.
  • Not a newsletter or chat tool. You can export lists and calendars and use them with the programs you already have.
  • Not software for large federations with many member clubs.

docs.title: Advantages and drawbacks at a glance
docs.text:
AdvantagesDrawbacks
  • No running costs, no subscription
  • Nothing technical to operate: no server, no database
  • Your data stays with you; cloud folders only ever see encrypted data
  • Works without internet, e.g. in the sports hall
  • Access rights are enforced technically: whoever may not see bank details never receives them
  • No lock-in: the data is an open SQLite file and can be exported at any time
  • Every board member has to install the program on their own device and keep it up to date
  • No access from a phone or a browser
  • Members can't maintain their own data
  • When working together, other people's changes arrive with a short delay
  • You are responsible for your own backups
  • Collaboration comes with an emergency key that must be stored safely

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Install: download and start the program
  • Set up: create the admin account, try the demo data
  • Members: the heart of the app
  • Switch from Excel: bring your existing lists along

docs.title: Login & password
docs.text:
Log in with the email address and password you set during setup or received from your administrator.

You stay logged in while the program is open, also when the page is reloaded. If the program is not used for more than 12 hours, or your password or role changes, the session ends: the login page shows "Your session has expired", and after logging in again you return to the page you were on. To log out, click your account at the bottom left of the sidebar → Logout.

docs.title: Changing your password
docs.text:
Not available yet

A profile page for changing your own password exists but cannot be reached from the menu yet. Until then, an administrator can delete your account in user management and create it again with a new password.

The new password must be at least 8 characters long.

Collaboration: your password protects the device key

When collaboration is turned on, your password also protects this device's key. Remember it well.

docs.title: Forgot password
docs.text:
Forgot password? sends you a reset link by email. This only works if email sending (SMTP) is configured for Open ClubManager, which is usually not the case in a normal desktop installation.

The link is valid for one hour and works only once; requesting a new one invalidates the old one. After the reset, all existing sessions of the account are signed out.

Without email sending:

  • You are not the only administrator: ask another administrator to delete your user account in user management and create it again.
  • You are the only administrator: restore a backup whose password you still know, or ask the community for help.

docs.title: First-run setup
docs.text: On first start there is no user account yet, so Open ClubManager guides you through setup in three steps.

docs.title: Step 1: Choose how you'll use it
docs.text:
Option When? Only on this device You manage the club on your own, or you just want to try it out. You can turn on collaboration at any time later. Together with others – set up a new club You are on the board and want several people to work with the same data. You first set up your account, then the shared club. Together with others – I have an invite Someone from the club sent you an invite code. Use the emergency key (small button at the bottom) All board devices are lost and you want to restore the club with the emergency key.

Click Next.

docs.title: Step 2: Choose the database
docs.text:
Enter where the database file should be stored, for example:

  • Windows: C:\Users\Name\Documents\clubmanager.db
  • macOS: /Users/name/Documents/clubmanager.db
  • Linux: /home/name/clubmanager.db

If the file doesn't exist yet, it is created. If you point to an existing Open ClubManager database, it is used.

Don't put it in a cloud folder

Do not put the database file into a Nextcloud, OneDrive, Dropbox or Google Drive folder or onto a network drive. It can get corrupted there while it is being synchronised. For working together, use collaboration, which is built exactly for this.

docs.title: Step 3: Create the admin account
docs.text:
Enter your email address and a password (at least 8 characters). This account has the role Administrator and may do everything.

Import demo data creates a fictional kitesurfing club with members, sections, events, inventory and transactions. Ideal for trying things out; leave it unticked for real use.

Note

Demo data is only available with "Only on this device", so that no made-up members are distributed to the whole board.

Click Create Admin Account. You are then taken to the login.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
From download to your first member in a few minutes:

  1. Install Open ClubManager for Windows, macOS or Linux.
  2. Set up: choose where the data is stored and create the first admin account. Optionally with demo data to try things out.
  3. Log in with your email and password.
  4. Get to know the interface: navigation, search, light and dark mode.
  5. Users and roles: add more people and decide who may do what.

Try first, then use real data

The first time, set up Open ClubManager with demo data (a fictional kitesurfing club). This lets you test every feature safely. For real use, create a new, empty database afterwards.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Open ClubManager is a desktop program. There is no web version: you install it on every computer you want to use it on.

docs.title: System requirements
docs.text: Minimum Windows Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) macOS macOS 11 Big Sur or later (Intel or Apple silicon) Linux a current distribution with WebKitGTK 4.1 (e.g. Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, Fedora 38+) Disk space about 50 MB for the program, plus a few MB for the club data Internet only for downloading, updates and collaboration

docs.title: Download
docs.text:
The installers are on the project's releases page.

No ready-made installers yet

Until the first version is released, there are no installers there yet. If you are technically inclined, you can build the program yourself; see the project README.

WindowsmacOSLinux
  1. Download Open ClubManager_x.y.z_x64-setup.exe (or the .msi).
  2. Double-click it and follow the installer.
  3. If Windows SmartScreen warns you ("Windows protected your PC"), click More info → Run anyway.
  4. Start Open ClubManager from the Start menu.
  1. Download Open ClubManager_x.y.z_universal.dmg.
  2. Open it and drag Open ClubManager into the Applications folder.
  3. On first start: right-click the app → Open, if macOS refuses to start it.
  • Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt install ./open-clubmanager_x.y.z_amd64.deb
  • Fedora/openSUSE: sudo dnf install ./open-clubmanager-x.y.z.x86_64.rpm
  • Others: make the .AppImage file executable (chmod +x) and run it.

docs.title: What gets installed?
docs.text:
Open ClubManager consists of the program window and a small background service that manages the data. The service starts and stops automatically with the window and can only be reached from your own computer.

Besides the program, Open ClubManager creates a configuration file:

Operating system Configuration location Windows %AppData%\open-clubmanager\config.json macOS ~/Library/Application Support/open-clubmanager/config.json Linux ~/.config/open-clubmanager/config.json

The club data itself lives in the database file whose location you choose during setup.

Turn on disk encryption

The database file is not additionally encrypted on your computer. Therefore turn on your operating system's encryption (Windows: BitLocker or device encryption, macOS: FileVault, Linux: LUKS). Especially on laptops, this protects member data if the device gets lost.

docs.title: Uninstalling
docs.text: Uninstall Open ClubManager like any other program. Your database file is kept. Delete it yourself if you no longer need it, and don't forget any backups.

docs.title: Sidebar
docs.text:
On the left you find all areas, grouped into:

  • Overview: the start page
  • Club: members, events, attendance, families & households, finances, inventory, anniversaries & honors, qualifications, tasks, club structure
  • Administration: history, users, collaboration, settings

You only see the areas your role may see. Finances, for example, are only visible to administrators and treasurers.

Use « at the bottom of the sidebar to collapse it for more space. At the bottom left you see which account and role you are logged in with.

docs.title: Search and quick actions
docs.text: Press Ctrl+K (macOS: Cmd+K) or click the magnifying glass at the top right. You can search for pages and members and start quick actions such as New member or Sync now. Use the arrow keys to select and Enter to open.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text: The bell at the top right shows when something needs your attention, for example inspections due in the inventory or conflicts to resolve in collaboration.

docs.title: Light and dark mode
docs.text: Use the moon or sun icon at the top right to switch between light and dark mode.

docs.title: Language
docs.text: Open ClubManager is available in German, English and French. Set the language in the settings.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text:
Many areas show data as a table. Everywhere:

  • Clicking a column header sorts.
  • The column menu (⋮) lets you filter and show or hide columns.
  • The checkboxes on the left select several entries, e.g. for deleting.

docs.title: Users & roles
docs.text:
Open ClubManager has two kinds of permissions that work together:

  1. User role: which account you log in with and what this account may do. Always applies.
  2. Device role: only with collaboration turned on: which data areas this device receives at all.

The stricter of the two always wins.

docs.title: User roles
docs.text:
Role May Administrator do everything, including user management Treasurer edit club data, see and edit finances Secretary edit club data, see and maintain qualifications; no finances Trainer view everything like "Read Only"; additionally record attendance for their own groups and sections Read Only view data, change nothing; no finances

"Club data" means members, club structure, inventory, events, households and tasks.

"No finances" means: no cash book, no fees or fee models, no direct debits, no payment reconciliation, no donation receipts – and no entries about them in the history.

How does Open ClubManager know a trainer's groups?

An account with the role Trainer is linked to a member by email address. The groups and sections of that member decide for which events the trainer may record attendance.

Create users in user management.

docs.title: Device roles in collaboration
docs.text:
Area Board Treasurer Secretary Coach Equipment manager Members edit view edit view view Contact details edit view edit – – Bank details edit edit – – – Finances edit edit – – – Inventory edit view view view edit Administration edit – – – –

"–" means: the device does not receive this data at all. It is transferred encrypted, and the device doesn't have the key. More under People & devices.

docs.title: Attendance
docs.text: Record who came to training and analyse participation.

docs.title: Recording attendance
docs.text:
1. At the top, choose the period (e.g. last 14 days) and, if needed, a group/section.
  2. Click an event. All members of the event's audience are listed.
  3. Mark each member as present, excused or unexcused. Rest present marks all remaining members at once.
  4. Add guest records people who don't belong to the audience.

Each card shows whether an event has been recorded ("3 of 12 present") or not yet.

Works offline too

If you have no connection in the hall and work with collaboration, the record is saved on the device and transferred automatically once the storage location is reachable again.

docs.title: Trainers
docs.text: Users with the role Trainer only see and record events of their own groups and sections. These come from the member with the same email address as the user account. See Users & roles.

docs.title: Statistics
docs.text:
The Statistics tab shows for any period:

  • the attendance rate over time as a chart
  • per member, the number of present / excused / unexcused and the rate

Use CSV or PDF to export the statistics, e.g. for grant applications or the annual general meeting.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text: Who takes care of what? Tasks for the board and for roles in the club.

docs.title: Adding a task
docs.text:
Click Add task and enter:

  • Title and description
  • Due: the due date
  • Assigned to: nobody, a member or a role (e.g. "Treasurer"). With a role, everybody who has that role is responsible.
  • Recurrence: once, weekly, monthly or yearly. Recurring tasks need a due date. When a recurring task is done, the next one is created automatically.
  • Linked member (optional), e.g. "Get the badge of honor for Anna"

docs.title: Status and filters
docs.text:
A task is Open, In progress or Done. Overdue tasks are highlighted.

The filters at the top show All, only Mine, only Overdue or only Done. Your open tasks are also shown on the overview.

Examples of recurring tasks

  • Yearly: prepare the fee collection, invite to the annual general meeting, apply for the sports grant
  • Monthly: import the bank statement
  • Weekly: return the hall key

docs.title: User management
docs.text: Here administrators create the accounts used to log in to this Open ClubManager.

docs.title: Creating a user
docs.text:
1. Click Create User.
  2. Enter the email address, an initial password (at least 8 characters) and the role.
  3. Share the login details with the person in a secure way.

Each email address can belong to only one account – the administrator's address from the setup can't be used a second time either. Upper and lower case don't matter.

docs.title: Changing the role and deleting users
docs.text:
Use the actions in the list to change the role or delete an account. Deleted accounts can no longer log in; their changes remain visible in the history.

Users or collaboration?

User accounts only apply to this one device, e.g. when several people share a club PC. If several people should work on their own devices, use collaboration.

docs.title: Overview (dashboard)
docs.text: The overview is your start page after logging in.

docs.title: What you see here
docs.text:
• Key figures: number of members (and how many are active), sections, groups, roles, and how many fees have been paid this year.
  • Quick access: straight to members, a new transaction, the club structure or the recent changes.
  • Upcoming events from the calendar.
  • Notice cards whenever there is something to do:
    • My tasks (open and overdue): see Tasks
    • Upcoming anniversaries: see Anniversaries & honors
    • Expiring qualifications: see Qualifications
    • Inspections & maintenance due: see Inventory
    • Households without a main payer: see Families & households
  • Statistics & charts: member development over the last 12 months, income and expenses, fee status and members per section.

Notice cards only appear when there really is something to show, and only for areas your role may see.

docs.title: Anniversaries & honors
docs.text: Never miss a round membership anniversary or birthday again, and keep track of who received which honor.

docs.title: Upcoming anniversaries
docs.text:
In the Upcoming tab, choose a period (From / To), e.g. up to the next annual general meeting. Open ClubManager lists all members who, in that period,

  • have a membership anniversary (e.g. 10, 25, 40, 50 years), calculated from the entry date, or
  • celebrate a round birthday (e.g. 50, 60, 70).

Set which milestones apply in the Membership years and Round birthdays fields (comma separated, e.g. 10, 25, 40, 50, 60).

Export as CSV gives you the list, e.g. for printing certificates.

docs.title: Recording an honor
docs.text: When a member has received an honor, click Record honor and enter e.g. "Silver badge of honor" and a note. Recorded honors are listed in the Recorded honors tab; that milestone is no longer suggested. If you delete an honor, the milestone is suggested again.

docs.title: Correcting membership years
docs.text: If a member left in between or the entry date is unknown, correct the membership years: the correction in years is added to the calculated years (e.g. -3 for a three-year break).

docs.title: Database path
docs.text: Shows which database file Open ClubManager uses. You can switch to another file here, e.g. after moving to a new computer. Open ClubManager checks whether the path is a valid database or whether one can be created there.

docs.title: Language
docs.text: German, English or French. The setting applies to this device.

docs.title: SEPA direct debit
docs.text:
Only visible to administrators and treasurers. Here you enter the details for collecting fees by direct debit:

  • Club name (creditor)
  • Creditor identifier, issued by your national bank, e.g. DE98ZZZ09999999999
  • IBAN of the club account and optionally the BIC (not needed for domestic payments)
  • Remittance template, with placeholders that are replaced by the member's and fee's data in each run

docs.title: Donation receipts
docs.text:
Only visible to administrators and treasurers. Here you enter the details for donation receipts after the official template:

  • club name and address, tax office and tax number
  • kind of notice (exemption notice or annex to the corporate tax assessment, or assessment under § 60a AO), its date and, for an exemption notice, the last assessment period
  • privileged purposes as in the notice
  • place and signatory for the signature line
  • whether membership fees are tax-deductible (not for sports clubs)

If the notice is older than 5 years (assessment under § 60a AO: 3 years), a warning appears.

docs.title: Collaboration
docs.text: A short status of collaboration and a link to its settings.

docs.title: Backup
docs.text:
You are responsible for backups

Open ClubManager only stores the data on your computer. If the disk fails or the laptop is stolen and there is no backup, the data is gone. With collaboration the other devices also have the data, but that still doesn't replace a backup.

docs.title: Creating a backup
docs.text:
Click Back up now. Open ClubManager creates a .zip file with the complete database. Below the button you see when the last backup was made.

Recommendations:

  • back up regularly, e.g. monthly and before every update
  • keep the backup in another place (USB stick, external drive, encrypted cloud storage)
  • protect the backup: it contains all member and bank data

docs.title: Restoring a backup
docs.text:
1. Click Select backup file (.zip) and choose the backup.
  2. Click Restore backup and confirm.
  3. Restart Open ClubManager.

Restoring overwrites the current data completely. If in doubt, back up the current state first.

docs.title: Finances
docs.text:
Cash book, member fees, fee models with automatic billing runs, open items, fee collection by SEPA direct debit, payment reconciliation with the bank statement and donation receipts. Only visible to administrators and treasurers.

At the top you see the balance, total income, total expenses and outstanding fees.

docs.title: Cash book
docs.text:
Every income and expense is a transaction with date, description, amount, type (income/expense), category and notes.

  • Add Transaction creates a new transaction.
  • Use the pencil and bin icons to edit or delete transactions.

Costs from maintenance in the inventory can be booked straight into the cash book as an expense.

docs.title: Importing a bank statement (CAMT.053)
docs.text:
Instead of typing every transaction, import your bank's statement in CAMT.053 format (XML). Most banks offer this in online banking, often under "export statement" or "export transactions → CAMT".

  1. Click Import CAMT.053 and select the file.
  2. Open ClubManager creates a transaction for every bank movement: credits as income, debits as expenses. The payer's name and IBAN and the direct debit references are kept for the payment reconciliation.
  3. Afterwards you see a summary of how many transactions were imported, and for how many there is a suggestion which open fee they pay. Open reconciliation takes you straight to the review.

Current limitations

Import each statement only once. Already imported movements are not detected yet and would be booked twice.

docs.title: Member fees
docs.text:
Here you manage the fees per member and year: amount, due date, paid date and description. Open fees are marked as Unpaid.

A fee counts as paid once you enter the paid date, a direct debit run is confirmed, or enough payments are assigned to it in the payment reconciliation. A partly paid fee stays unpaid until the rest arrives.

Add single fees (e.g. an admission fee) with Add Member Fee. The regular fees of all members are better created at once from fee models with a billing run.

docs.title: Open items
docs.text: The Open items tab shows all unpaid fees, grouped per member: number of fees, open amount, oldest due date and which fees they are. At the top you see the total open amount, how much of it is overdue and how many members have open items. Overdue items are marked red. Members with the highest open amount come first.

docs.title: Fee models
docs.text:
A fee model is one of your club's fee classes, e.g. adults, youth, family, passive or reduced. Create them in the Fee models tab with Add fee model:

Field Meaning Name Used in the description of the created fees, e.g. "Adults 2027". Must be unique. Amount Amount per period of the interval (for quarterly, the quarterly fee). Interval yearly, half-yearly, quarterly or monthly. Periods follow the calendar year (first half = January–June, first quarter = January–March, …). Minimum / maximum age Optional. Models with an age limit are assigned automatically by age (see below). Both limits are inclusive: maximum age 17 means "up to and including 17". Pro rata When members join or leave during a period, charge only the months of membership (see Pro rata).

A changed amount applies to all future billing runs; fees already created stay unchanged.

docs.title: Which member pays which model?
docs.text:
Member assignments lists all current members with their age on 1 January and the fee they pay this year. Change the assignment right in the list or in the member dialog under Membership → Fee model:

  • Automatic by age (default): the member gets the model with an age limit that fits their age. If several fit, the one with the narrowest age range wins (e.g. students 18–27 before adults 18 and over).
  • A specific model, e.g. family or passive: applies regardless of age.
  • Exempt from fees, e.g. for honorary members: the member gets no fees.

Coming of age

What counts is the age on 1 January of the fee year. A member who turns 18 in June still pays the youth fee that year and the adult fee automatically from the next year. This way the change never leaves a gap or charges twice, even if the two models have different intervals.

Members without a birthday or without a matching model are marked yellow and skipped by billing runs. When a model is deleted, its members get their model by age again.

docs.title: Billing run
docs.text:
A billing run creates the fees of all members for a range at once, typically at the start of the year for the whole year.

  1. In the Billing run tab, choose the range: From (month) and To (month), e.g. January to December 2027. All fee periods that start in these months are charged.
  2. Set Due on, e.g. 1 March. Periods that start later (e.g. the third quarter) are due when they start.
  3. Click Preview. Nothing is saved yet. The preview shows the number and total of the fees, every single fee with amount and due date, and below who is skipped and why:
    • already charged: the member already has a fee from a billing run for this period,
    • without a matching fee model: e.g. the birthday is missing,
    • exempt from fees.
  4. If everything is right, Save billing run. The fees appear under Member fees and Open items and can be collected by direct debit as usual.

Previous billing runs lists every saved run with the number of fees, the total and how many fees are already paid.

docs.title: No duplicate fees
docs.text:
Open ClubManager records which period every created fee is for. A period that has already been charged to a member is never charged a second time:

  • If you start the same billing run again, the preview shows "nothing to charge" and saving is refused.
  • If the range overlaps an earlier run, only the missing periods are charged. So you can, for example, repeat the run in summer to charge members who joined since.
  • If you delete a created fee, its period is free again and can be charged again.

Fees added by hand

This only applies to fees from a billing run. If you have already added fees of a period by hand with Add Member Fee (e.g. the yearly fee before switching to fee models), they would be charged a second time. Start the first billing run with the next period, or delete the open fees added by hand first.

To undo a billing run created by mistake, use the bin icon in Previous billing runs: all open fees of the run are deleted, paid ones stay. If fees are in a direct debit run that has not been confirmed, cancel or confirm that run first.

docs.title: Joining and leaving
docs.text:
• Members who left are no longer charged from their exit date: periods that start on or after the exit date get no fee. On the exit date itself the person is no longer a member.
  • Members who join only after a period has ended get no fee for that period.

docs.title: Pro rata
docs.text:
Without the Pro rata option, the full amount is due for a period as soon as the person is a member on at least one day of it. With Pro rata, every month of the period counts in which the person is a member on at least one day; the corresponding share is charged, rounded to the cent.

Example (yearly fee €120, pro rata) Months Fee Joins on 1 or 30 April April–December = 9 €90.00 Leaves on 1 July (last day: 30 June) January–June = 6 €60.00 Joins 15 March, leaves 20 August March–August = 6 €60.00

In the preview, pro rata fees are marked "pro rata of …".

docs.title: Direct debit (SEPA)
docs.text: In the Direct debit tab you collect open fees by SEPA Core direct debit. Open ClubManager creates a file in the pain.008 bank format that you upload in online banking. The tab only appears if your role may edit finances and, with collaboration, your device receives bank and finance data.

docs.title: One-time setup
docs.text:
1. In the settings under SEPA direct debit, enter the club name, the creditor identifier (issued by your national bank, e.g. DE98ZZZ09999999999), the IBAN of the club account and optionally a remittance template.
  2. For every member who pays by direct debit, enter the IBAN, SEPA Mandate Date and a unique mandate reference (e.g. NW-1001) under Bank Details in the member dialog.

docs.title: Creating a direct debit run
docs.text:
Click Create direct debit run. A wizard guides you through three steps:

  1. Select fees: all open fees are listed; partly paid fees with the amount still due. Fees that can't be collected (no IBAN, no mandate, no mandate reference, invalid IBAN …) are listed under Cannot be collected with the reason; complete the member's data.
  2. Due date & remittance: the collection date. The file must reach the bank at least one business day before. Below it you see a preview of the remittance text.
  3. Review & export: check the count, total, first (FRST) and recurring (RCUR) collections, then click Create & download.

The fees are then marked as Being collected.

docs.title: After the export
docs.text:
Step Where Upload the .xml file in online banking and authorise it at your bank Once the bank has collected: Confirm as paid and enter the date; all fees of the run are marked as paid the run in the list Returned debits: import the bank statement and confirm them in the reconciliation; the fee is open again and can be collected once more Payment reconciliation Created a run by mistake? Cancel run and the fees are open again. Then don't upload the file, or revoke the order at the bank the run in the list

Download XML file gives you a run's file again.

First and recurring collections

When a mandate is used for the first time, Open ClubManager marks the debit as a first collection (FRST), afterwards as recurring (RCUR). This happens automatically.

docs.title: Payment reconciliation
docs.text: In the Reconciliation tab you assign imported incoming payments to open fees instead of looking up every transfer by hand. Open ClubManager suggests which fees each transaction pays; nothing is booked until you confirm. Like direct debit, the tab only appears if your role may edit finances and your device receives bank and finance data.

docs.title: How suggestions are made
docs.text:
For every incoming payment Open ClubManager checks:

  • the member number in the remittance text, e.g. "Fee 2026 member 1013" or "No. 12" (short numbers only with a word such as "Mitglied", "member", "Nr.", "No." or "#" in front),
  • the payer's IBAN against the members' bank details,
  • the name of the payer and in the remittance text, also with umlauts ("Möller" = "Moeller") and small typos,
  • the amount: does it match one open fee, all open fees of the member, or of their household?

This gives the match quality:

Match quality Meaning Certain Member number or IBAN recognised and the amount matches exactly Probable Member number or IBAN recognised but the amount differs (partial or overpayment), or name and amount match Unclear Only the name matches, not the amount; check carefully No suggestion No matching open fee, e.g. for donations or sponsoring

The chips below a suggestion show what it was recognised by (e.g. Member number, IBAN, Amount matches, Household, Partial payment).

docs.title: Reviewing and confirming
docs.text:
• Confirm (tick) takes over the suggestion. The fee gets the booking date as paid date.
  • Confirm all certain takes over all suggestions rated Certain at once.
  • Change assignment (pencil) opens a searchable list of all open fees. Tick the right fees and adjust the amounts; this is how you correct a suggestion or assign a transaction without one yourself.
  • Mark as reviewed without fee is for a transaction that pays no fee (e.g. a donation). It disappears from the open transactions.
  • Undo (under Done) takes an assignment back. The fees return to their previous state.

docs.title: Partial payments and collective transfers
docs.text:
• If a member pays in instalments, assign every instalment to the same fee. The fee stays Unpaid until the total is reached; a direct debit then only collects the rest.
  • If parents pay for several children at once, the suggestion splits the amount across the household's fees. In the dialog you can pick any number of fees, also of different members, each with its own amount.
  • If an overpayment leaves a rest, it is shown and not assigned to any fee.

docs.title: Returned direct debits
docs.text:
Open ClubManager recognises a returned direct debit on import by its bank code or return reason and shows it in red with the reason, e.g. Insufficient funds or Refund requested by payer. The suggestion names the fee that had been paid: reliably by the debit reference for runs created in Open ClubManager, otherwise by IBAN, member number and amount.

When you confirm the returned debit, the fee is open again and can be collected in a new direct debit run. Bank charges for the return remain as a rest without fee.

Trying it with the demo data

If you chose the demo data during setup, you can try the reconciliation with the example file testdata/camt053-reconciliation.xml: it contains certain, probable and unclear payments, a family transfer, a returned direct debit and a sponsoring income.

docs.title: Donation receipts
docs.text:
Charitable clubs in Germany may issue donation receipts (Zuwendungsbestätigungen) for donations (and, depending on their purposes, membership fees), which donors use to deduct the donation from their taxes. Open ClubManager creates them as PDF after the official template of the Federal Ministry of Finance – as a single receipt or as a collective receipt with annex. Administrators and treasurers see the Donations tab when their device receives the finances and the members' addresses.

The club is liable for correct receipts

Whoever issues a wrong donation receipt intentionally or through gross negligence is liable for the lost tax (§ 10b (4) EStG). Check donor, amount and date before you issue a receipt. When in doubt, ask your tax adviser or the tax office.

docs.title: One-time setup
docs.text:
Enter the data of your tax office notice in the settings: club name and address, tax office, tax number, kind and date of the notice and the privileged purposes exactly as in the notice (in German, e.g. "des Sports (§ 52 Abs. 2 Satz 1 Nr. 21 AO)").

Kind of notice Valid for receipts Exemption notice (Freistellungsbescheid) or annex to the corporate tax assessment 5 years from the date of the notice Assessment under § 60a AO (e.g. for a newly founded club) 3 years from the date of the notice

If the notice is older, the tax office no longer recognises the receipts (§ 63 (5) AO). Open ClubManager then shows a warning in the settings and in the tab, with the date until which the notice was valid.

Membership fees

For sports clubs and clubs with leisure purposes (e.g. culture of a leisure nature, local heritage, allotments) membership fees are not deductible (§ 10b (1) sentence 8 EStG). Leave the switch Membership fees are tax-deductible off: only donations are certified, and the receipt confirms that it is not a membership fee. With the switch on, the paid fees of the year are listed as well.

docs.title: Recording donations
docs.text:
A donation is an income in the cash book with the category Spende (or "Spenden"). Donations → Donations lists all such incomes.

  1. Click the pencil next to a donation and choose the member or an external donor. Add external donors (e.g. companies) below under External donors or right in the dialog.
  2. Tick Waiver of reimbursement of expenses for an expense donation, i.e. when someone waives the reimbursement of travel costs or similar.
  3. An income without a category gets the category "Spende" when you assign it.

A receipt needs the donor's complete address (street, postal code and town). For members it comes from their contact details.

docs.title: Issuing receipts
docs.text:
Under Donations → Issue receipts choose the year and the issue date. The list shows every donor with their donations of the year; items already certified are marked with the receipt number.

  • Single receipt certifies exactly one donation.
  • Collective receipt combines all open donations of a donor in the year. The annex lists each donation with date, kind and amount.
  • Annual run creates the missing receipts for all donors of the year at once – a collective receipt for several donations, a single receipt otherwise. Donors without a complete address are skipped and named.

The PDFs are downloaded right away (for the annual run all in one file, each receipt starting on a new page). Print and sign them.

docs.title: Numbering, log and duplicates
docs.text:
Every receipt gets a sequential number per year, e.g. 2026-0001. Donations → Log shows which receipt was issued when, for whom and by whom.

  • A donation can be certified only once. If you create a receipt for the same donations again – or click Create duplicate in the log – you get a duplicate with the same number, clearly marked DUPLIKAT on the PDF, which is logged as well.
  • If a receipt was wrong (e.g. wrong amount), void it with a reason. It stays in the log and is marked as voided on the PDF; its donations can then be certified again. A certified donation can only be assigned to another donor after the receipt was voided.

docs.title: Deleting the full ledger
docs.text:
For a fresh start (e.g. after trying things out with demo data) you can delete all transactions, fees and billing runs at once; fee models and member assignments stay. For safety you have to type a confirmation word. This cannot be undone; create a backup first.

Not a replacement for accounting

The cash book is a helper for everyday club life. It does not replace tax-compliant bookkeeping, accounting exports or advice from tax advisors or auditors.

docs.title: Families & households
docs.text: Group members who live together or pay together into a household, typically for family memberships.

docs.title: Adding a household
docs.text:
1. Click Add household.
  2. Enter a name, e.g. "Miller family".
  3. Select the members. A member can only belong to one household.
  4. Choose the main payer. They pay the fees for the whole household (e.g. by direct debit).
  5. Optional: Shared address and/or Shared bank details. The main payer's details are then used for all members of the household. If one member's address changes, it changes for all.

Deleting a household keeps its members.

docs.title: When the main payer leaves
docs.text: If the main payer leaves the club, Open ClubManager warns you that the remaining members would have no main payer. Choose a new main payer in the household. Households without an active main payer also appear as a notice on the overview.

docs.title: Guardians
docs.text:
In the member dialog under Family & guardians you record the guardians of minors:

  • Club member: a guardian who is a member themselves
  • Other person: with name and relationship (e.g. "mother")

If a member is a minor and has no guardians, Open ClubManager points this out.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
All areas of Open ClubManager at a glance. Which ones you see depends on your role.

Area Purpose Overview Key figures, upcoming events, due tasks and notices at a glance Members Master data, addresses, bank details & SEPA, import/export, GDPR data export Families & households Households with a main payer, guardians Events Club calendar with recurring events and calendar export Attendance Record and analyse training attendance Finances Cash book, member fees, fee models & billing runs, open items, SEPA direct debit, bank statement import, payment reconciliation, donation receipts Inventory Items, loans, inspections and maintenance Anniversaries & honors Membership anniversaries, round birthdays, honors Qualifications Licences, first aid, police clearance certificates with expiry warnings Tasks Who takes care of what Club structure Sections, groups and roles History Who changed what and when User management Accounts and user roles Settings Language, database, backup

docs.title: Inventory
docs.text: Keep track of the club's equipment: what you have, where it is, who borrowed it and when it needs an inspection.

docs.title: Items
docs.text:
Add item records name, description, serial number, category, quantity, location, purchase date and purchase price.

The search field and the category filter help you find items quickly. Only due shows only items whose inspection is due soon or overdue.

docs.title: Loans
docs.text:
1. Click Create loan.
  2. Choose the item and the member, the loan date and optionally a due date.
  3. On return: Mark as returned.

At the top you see all currently loaned items. Only items in condition Ready can be lent out.

docs.title: Inspection & maintenance
docs.text:
For equipment that must be inspected regularly (life jackets, climbing ropes, first-aid kits, sports equipment), open Inspection & maintenance on the item:

  • Condition: Ready, Damaged, In repair or Retired
  • Interval (months): how often it must be inspected
  • Next inspection: moves forward by the interval automatically after each recorded inspection

Record inspection / maintenance documents the date, who did it, cost, a note and the condition afterwards. Tick the box to book the cost directly as an expense in the cash book.

In the list, a badge shows the inspection status: On schedule, Due soon or Overdue. Due inspections also appear on the overview.

The maintenance history lists all past inspections, useful as evidence for insurers, for example.

docs.title: Members
docs.text: Member management is the heart of Open ClubManager.

docs.title: Member list
docs.text:
The table shows all members. The search field finds members by name, email or membership number. Use the column headers to sort and filter; hide columns you don't need (e.g. IBAN) via the column menu.

Above the table are the actions for the selected members:

Icon Action Edit the selected member Delete the selected members Create a data export for the selected member Export the member list as an Excel file Import members from an Excel file

docs.title: Adding or editing a member
docs.text:
Click Add Member, or select a member and click the pencil icon.

The details are grouped into collapsible sections:

Section Content Personal Information membership number, email (required), first and last name, birthday, phone, mobile, comment Address street, postal code, city, state Bank Details account holder, IBAN, BIC, bank, date of the SEPA mandate, mandate reference (for direct debit, up to 35 characters without spaces, unique) Membership entry and exit date; for existing members the fee model (automatic by age, a specific model or exempt; only administrators and treasurers may change it) Club Entities assignment to sections, groups and roles Family & guardians household and guardians (for minors)

Input checks

When saving, Open ClubManager checks the details and marks invalid fields right in the dialog: first and last name are required, the membership number must be 1 or higher, the IBAN must have the length of its country and correct check digits (spaces and lower case don't matter), a BIC must have 8 or 11 characters, the exit date cannot be before the entry date and the birthday cannot be in the future. Texts are limited in length (names 100, comment 2000 characters).

Membership numbers

Membership numbers and email addresses must be unique. With collaboration, two people may assign the same number at the same time; this then shows up under Needs attention.

docs.title: Leaving and deleting members
docs.text:
• Leaving the club: enter an exit date. The member is kept and counts as an exit in the statistics.
  • Deleting: removes the member completely. Use this when the data no longer has to be kept (data protection: don't store data longer than necessary).

docs.title: Excel import
docs.text:
The import brings in existing member lists. Described in detail under Switching from Excel.

  1. Select the Excel file (.xlsx).
  2. Assign columns: map each column of your file to a field in Open ClubManager or choose "Ignore". Choose whether existing members are recognised and updated by email or membership number.
  3. Check the preview: duplicate values are highlighted. Then import.

docs.title: Excel export
docs.text:
Exports the member list as memberlist.xlsx, e.g. for mail merges or as a list for the annual general meeting.

Exported files are not protected

An exported Excel file contains personal data and is no longer protected by Open ClubManager. Only pass it on when necessary, and delete it when you no longer need it.

docs.title: Data export (GDPR)
docs.text:
Every member has the right to know what data the club stores about them (Art. 15 GDPR) and to receive it in a machine-readable format (Art. 20 GDPR).

Select the member and click the shield icon → Create data export:

  • Readable report (PDF): to print or send to the member
  • Machine-readable data (JSON): for data portability

More under Data protection.

docs.title: Qualifications & licences
docs.text: Coaching licences, first-aid courses, trainer certificates and police clearance certificates, with a warning before anything expires. Only visible to administrators and secretaries.

docs.title: Adding types
docs.text:
In the Types tab, first define which qualifications your club tracks, for example:

Type Validity Coaching licence level C 48 months First-aid course 24 months Enhanced police clearance certificate 60 months, inspection date only Boat licence empty (unlimited)

If the validity is left empty, the qualification does not expire.

docs.title: Recording a qualification
docs.text:
Click Record qualification, choose the member and type and enter the issue date. The expiry date is calculated from the validity; you can override it.

The status shows Valid, Expires soon or Expired. Qualifications that expire soon also appear on the overview.

docs.title: Police clearance certificates (§ 72a SGB VIII)
docs.text: In Germany, clubs working with children and young people must inspect enhanced police clearance certificates but may not store their content. So enable Store inspection date only for that type. Then only the fact that and when the certificate was inspected is recorded. Notes are disabled for this type.

docs.title: Events
docs.text: The club calendar for training sessions, festivals, meetings and competitions.

docs.title: Views
docs.text: At the top right, switch between Month, Week and List. The arrows page through time, Today jumps back to the current date. Audience shows only events of certain groups, sections or roles.

docs.title: Adding an event
docs.text:
Click Add event and fill in:

Field Note Title and category Training, Festival, Meeting, Competition or Other; the category sets the colour in the calendar All day for multi-day events such as tournaments or camps Start / End Recurrence never, weekly, every 2 weeks or monthly; with Repeat until (empty = no end) Location and description Groups, sections, roles the audience; without a selection the event is for the whole club

The audience also decides who is expected as a participant in attendance.

docs.title: Editing recurring events
docs.text:
For recurring events you can choose:

  • Edit series: changes all events of the series
  • Remove only this date: skips a single date (e.g. no training during school holidays)
  • Delete series: removes the whole series

docs.title: Exporting the calendar
docs.text:
• Export calendar (.ics) exports all events, for importing into Outlook, Google Calendar, Apple Calendar or Thunderbird.
  • For a single event, Download .ics downloads only that event, e.g. to email it to members.

Note

The export is a snapshot. A subscribable online calendar isn't possible because Open ClubManager is not a web application.

docs.title: Club structure
docs.text:
Sections, groups and roles make up your club's structure. Members can belong to several of them.

Purpose Examples Sections the club's divisions; help to differentiate fees and split statistics football, gymnastics, kite, foil Groups thematic or organisational groups training groups, age groups, project teams, adults, youth (U18) Roles members' positions and offices board, treasurer, coach, youth officer

Roles here ≠ user roles

The roles of the club structure describe positions in the club. They grant no permissions in the program. What someone may do in the program is decided by their user role.

docs.title: Adding and editing
docs.text: Choose the tab at the top (groups, roles or sections) and click Create New …. Enter a name and description.

docs.title: Assigning members
docs.text:
Click the people icon (Assign members) on an entry. Search for members and tick them, so you can assign many members at once. Single assignments can also be changed in the member dialog under Club Entities.

Groups, sections and roles are also used as the audience of events and for assigning tasks.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The history shows who changed what and when.

Each entry contains:

Column Content Timestamp when the change was made Action CREATE, UPDATE or DELETE Entity what was changed, e.g. Member, Event, InventoryLoan ID the internal identifier of the entry User who made the change Details further information about the change

The history helps with questions ("Who changed the address?") and as evidence for auditors. It cannot be edited.

Entries about finances – transactions, fees and fee models, direct debits, payment reconciliation and donation receipts – are only shown to roles that may see the finances (Administrator and Treasurer). See Users & roles.

docs.title: General
docs.text:
Does Open ClubManager cost anything?

No. Open ClubManager is free software under the AGPL-3.0 license. There is no paid version, no member limit and no subscription.

Is there a web version or a mobile app?

No, and none is planned. Open ClubManager is a desktop program by design: the data stays on your devices and nobody has to run a server. The downside: without a computer that has Open ClubManager installed, you can't get to the data.

Can members change their own data?

No. Open ClubManager is meant for the club's volunteers, not for the members themselves.

How many members can Open ClubManager handle?

It is designed for clubs with a few dozen to a few thousand members. The database (SQLite) can handle far more.

Do I need the internet?

Only for downloading, updates and collaboration. In "Only on this device" mode you work completely offline.

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
Where is my data?

In the database file whose location you chose during setup. You can see the path in the settings.

Can I put the database file in my Dropbox/OneDrive folder so others can access it?

Please don't. Simultaneous synchronisation can corrupt the file, and anyone with access to the folder could read all the data. Use collaboration instead: it only puts encrypted change files into the folder.

What happens if the project is discontinued?

The installed program keeps working. Your data is in an open SQLite file and can be exported at any time. See Exporting your data.

How do I back up my data?

Via Settings → Data Backup → Back up now. See Backup.

docs.title: Collaboration
docs.text:
I don't see my colleague's changes.

Check that your cloud provider's sync program is running and the folder is up to date. Then click Synchronize now in the sync status. Other people's data only arrives once your sync program has downloaded it.

Can I manage several clubs?

Not with collaboration at the moment: one club per device is supported. In local mode you can switch between database files in the settings.

A laptop was stolen. What should I do?

Remove the device immediately under People & devices and check whether you need to notify the data protection authority (72 hours, Art. 33 GDPR).

docs.title: Reporting problems
docs.text: Found a bug or have an idea? Get in touch via the issue tracker on GitHub. Please don't include real member data.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Term Meaning CAMT.053 Standard format for electronic bank statements (XML), offered by almost all banks. Collective receipt A donation receipt covering several donations of a year, with an annex (Sammelbestätigung). Conflict / to resolve Unique values assigned twice during collaboration. See Needs attention. Database file The file (.db) that stores all club data on your computer (SQLite format). Device role In collaboration: which data areas a device receives (board, treasurer, secretary, coach, equipment manager). Donation receipt Receipt after the official German template (Zuwendungsbestätigung) with which donors deduct a donation from their taxes. See Donation receipts. Emergency key Text for restoring administration when no board device is left. See Emergency key. Exemption notice Tax office notice that the club is charitable and exempt from corporate tax (Freistellungsbescheid). Basis for donation receipts; valid for 5 years. Group Thematic or organisational group of members, e.g. a training group. Invite code 24-character code a new device uses to join a club. Valid for 7 days, usable once. Main payer Member who pays the fees of a household. Migration (database) Automatic adjustment of the database to a new program version on start. See Updates. Returned direct debit A direct debit that the member's bank sends back, e.g. for insufficient funds. See Payment reconciliation. Role (club structure) A member's position in the club, e.g. youth officer. Grants no permissions in the program. Safety code 6-digit code a joining person tells the board so the board can approve the join request. Section A division of the club, e.g. football or gymnastics. See Club structure. SEPA mandate A member's authorisation to collect fees by direct debit. Shared folder / storage location The cloud or network folder through which devices exchange changes in collaboration. Sync Exchange of changes between the devices in collaboration. User role What a login account may do in the program (Administrator, Treasurer, Secretary, Trainer, Read Only).

docs.title: Exporting your data
docs.text:
Your data belongs to the club. You can get it out of Open ClubManager at any time, also when switching to other software.

What How Format Member list Members → export Excel (.xlsx) One member's data Data export PDF and JSON Events Export calendar iCalendar (.ics) Attendance Export statistics CSV, PDF Anniversaries Export as CSV CSV Everything Backup ZIP containing the SQLite database

docs.title: Opening the database directly
docs.text:
The database file is a regular SQLite database. Free tools like DB Browser for SQLite can open it and export every table as CSV, even without Open ClubManager. That's the way to do a complete move to other software.

The table structure is described in the data model.

Warning

Only open the database while Open ClubManager is closed, and preferably work on a copy. Editing the database directly is not supported and can cause inconsistencies with collaboration.

docs.title: Switching & migration
docs.text:
This section covers every situation in which data moves from A to B:

Situation Page You manage the club with spreadsheets today Switching from Excel You use other club software From other club software A new version of Open ClubManager is out Updates & database versions You get a new computer Moving to a new computer Until now alone, now the board should join in From local to collaboration You want to leave Open ClubManager or hand data over Exporting your data A version exceptionally needs manual steps Release notes

docs.title: Ground rules for every migration
docs.text:
1. Back up first. Create a backup and keep it until everything has been checked.
  2. Test first. Try the switch with a copy or a test database before working with real data.
  3. Check afterwards. Take samples: is the member count right? Are bank details and entry dates right for a few members?
  4. Delete old data securely. Don't leave old spreadsheets and exports with member data lying around forever.

docs.title: From local to collaboration
docs.text: You have used Open ClubManager on your own so far, and now the board should work with it too. Your existing data is carried over.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Create a backup.
  2. Tidy up: remove test data, merge duplicate members. Everything in the database now will be distributed to everyone.
  3. Collaboration → Turn on collaboration and set up the club. The data on this device becomes the club's starting state.
  4. Print the emergency key and store it safely.
  5. Invite the others.

Joining devices lose their local data

Anyone who joins and already has their own club data on their device (e.g. because they also used Open ClubManager on their own) receives the club's data, and their local data is replaced (a backup is created automatically). So merge several local datasets beforehand on the device that sets up the club, e.g. via Excel export and import.

docs.title: User accounts
docs.text: User accounts from user management only apply to this device and are not transferred. Each person logs in on their own device with their own account; what their device may see is decided by the device role.

docs.title: Back to local?
docs.text: Turning collaboration off is not supported at the moment. If you want to work alone again, take a backup of the current state and restore it on a device without collaboration, or export the members to Excel.

docs.title: Without collaboration (only on this device)
docs.text:
1. Old computer: create a backup and copy the .zip file to a USB stick.
  2. New computer: install Open ClubManager in the same or a newer version.
  3. Run first-run setup with "Only on this device" and create a temporary admin account (without demo data).
  4. Settings → Restore backup → choose the backup → confirm.
  5. Restart Open ClubManager and log in with your previous account.
  6. Take samples. If everything is right: securely delete the database and backup on the old computer.

Alternative: copy the file

You can also copy the database file (.db) directly and enter it as the database path during setup on the new computer. Close Open ClubManager on the old computer first.

docs.title: With collaboration
docs.text:
With collaboration, a new computer is simply a new device:

  1. Have the board invite you (or, as board, invite yourself).
  2. Join on the new computer. The data comes from the shared folder.
  3. Remove the old device under People & devices (reason: "Device is no longer used").

Before removing it, wait until the old device shows "Everything is in sync"; otherwise changes still waiting there are lost.

docs.title: Installing an update
docs.text:
1. Create a backup (Settings → Back up now).
  2. Close Open ClubManager.
  3. Download the new version from the releases page and install it over the old version. Your database file and settings are kept.
  4. Start Open ClubManager.
  5. Check the release notes to see whether the new version needs manual steps (rare).

docs.title: What happens on first start
docs.text:
New versions sometimes bring features that need the database to be extended (e.g. new tables for households or events). This database migration runs automatically on start:

  • You don't have to do anything.
  • Existing data is not deleted, it is carried over.
  • With large databases, the first start may take a few seconds longer.
Version 1.2 → 1.3 → 1.4
  database    step 13      step 14   (run one after another on start)

You can also skip versions: updating from 1.1 straight to 1.4 is no problem, all missing steps run one after another.

docs.title: Going back to the old version?
docs.text:
After a migration, an older program version can no longer reliably open the database. To go back:

  1. Install the older version.
  2. Restore the backup from before the update.

Changes you made after the update are lost.

docs.title: Updates with collaboration
docs.text:
With collaboration, all devices exchange changes in a shared format. Therefore:

  • Update all devices promptly. A device with an older version does not accept changes from newer versions and asks for an update. Its own changes are not lost; they are transferred once it is updated.
  • Newer versions always understand changes from older versions.
  • Agree within the board who updates first. Ideally everyone within a few days.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
