docs.text: • If the program doesn't start after the update or shows a database error: don't delete anything, keep the backup at hand and report it in the issue tracker (without real member data).

docs.title: Release notes
docs.text:
Normally an update needs no manual steps: the database is adjusted automatically on start.

If a version exceptionally needs a manual step (e.g. because an export format changes, a setting has to be set again, or with collaboration all devices must update at the same time), you'll find instructions here.

Currently no manual steps needed

So far no version has required manual steps when updating.

The full list of changes in each version is on the releases page.

docs.title: Switching from other club software
docs.text: There is no direct import from other club programs yet. The way in is an Excel file: almost every club program can export its member list as Excel or CSV.

docs.title: General procedure
docs.text:
1. Export from the old software: export the member list with all fields as Excel (.xlsx) or CSV. Include bank details and SEPA mandates if you use direct debits.
  2. Open the CSV in Excel/LibreOffice and save it as .xlsx. Watch the character encoding (UTF-8) when opening, so accented characters come out right.
  3. Prepare it as described under Switching from Excel.
  4. Import and check.
  5. Run in parallel: keep the old software running read-only for a while (e.g. until the next fee collection) before cancelling it.

docs.title: What cannot be transferred
docs.text:
• Transaction history of past years: close the old financial year in the old software and start in Open ClubManager with the opening balance.
  • Documents and attachments (scans, membership applications): Open ClubManager doesn't store files. Keep them in the club archive.
  • Online access for members: doesn't exist in Open ClubManager.

docs.title: Guides for specific programs
docs.text:
Ready for community contributions

This is where we collect step-by-step guides for individual programs. You switched from another software? Add a guide; the template is below and in Maintaining the documentation.

Software Status none yet – Template for a guide 
### From <name of the software>

**Tested with:** <version of the old software>, Open ClubManager <version>

1. Export: <menu path in the old software>, format <xlsx/csv>
2. File specifics: <separator, encoding, date format>
3. Column mapping:

| Column in the export | Field in Open ClubManager |
|---|---|
| … | … |

4. What's missing / follow-up: <…>

docs.title: Switching from Excel
docs.text: Most clubs start with a member list in a spreadsheet. The import brings it in within minutes.

docs.title: 1. Preparing the Excel list
docs.text:
Open ClubManager reads .xlsx files. The first row must contain the column headers, followed by one member per row.

Field in Open ClubManager Typical column in your list Membership number (number) Member no. First name (firstName), last name (lastName) First name, Surname Email (email) – required Email Phone (phone), mobile (phoneMobile) Phone, Mobile Birthday (birthday) Date of birth Street (street), postal code (postalCode), city (city), state (state) Address Entry date (entryDate), exit date (exitDate) Joined, Left Account holder (accountHolder), IBAN (iban), BIC (bic), bank (bankName) Bank details SEPA mandate date (sepaMandateDate) Mandate dated Comment (comment) Notes

Tips:

  • One column per field. If "street, postal code city" is in one cell, split it first in your spreadsheet (Data → Text to columns).
  • Format dates as real spreadsheet dates, not as text.
  • Email is required. Members without an email address get a unique placeholder (e.g. member-1042@club.invalid) that you replace later.
  • Membership numbers and email addresses must be unique. Duplicates are highlighted in the preview.
  • If your columns are named exactly like the field names in brackets, Open ClubManager maps them automatically.

docs.title: 2. Running the import
docs.text:
1. Members → import icon () → Select Excel-File.
  2. Assign columns: choose the matching field for each column of your file, or "Ignore".
  3. Update existing members by: email or membership number. For the first import it doesn't matter; for a later re-import, existing members are updated instead of duplicated.
  4. Check the preview and import.

Rows with invalid details (e.g. a missing name or an IBAN with wrong check digits, see input checks) are skipped; the other rows are imported. A notification then lists which rows are missing and why. Fix them in the file and import again.

docs.title: 3. Follow-up
docs.text:
• Create sections, groups and roles in the club structure and assign them in bulk via Assign members.
  • Create households for family memberships (Families & households).
  • Record the current year's fees under Finances → Member Fees.
  • Take samples, then archive or securely delete the old spreadsheet.

docs.title: Other lists
docs.text: Spreadsheet Where it goes Cash book Start fresh from a cut-off date; record the opening balance as one income transaction; bank movements via CAMT.053 import Inventory list enter in Inventory (no import yet) Schedule in Events; create training sessions as a series Licences / first-aid list in Qualifications

docs.title: Maintaining the documentation
docs.text: This guide grows with every new feature. This page is for everyone contributing to Open ClubManager.

docs.title: Principle
docs.text: Every user-visible feature is documented, in both languages, in the same pull request. CI checks this automatically.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
mkdocs.yml                         configuration, navigation and nav translations
docs/requirements.txt              versions of MkDocs, Material theme and i18n plugin
docs/user/                         source of this guide
  page.md                          German page (default language, served at /)
  page.en.md                       English translation (served at /en/)
  assets/screenshots/              generated screenshots: name.png (German), name.en.png (English)
docs/templates/migration-guide.md  template for release notes with manual steps
scripts/check_docs_coverage.py     checks that every page of the app is documented in both languages
scripts/docs-screenshots/          generates the screenshots with Playwright

docs.title: What happens automatically
docs.text: When What Where Every pull request Check: every route of the app (frontend/src/routes/routes.tsx) is listed in the front matter of exactly one page per language; every page has its translation; every screenshot is used; mkdocs build --strict finds no broken links docs job in .github/workflows/ci.yml Push to main (app changed) Screenshots are regenerated in both languages; if they changed, they are committed straight to main and the docs are republished .github/workflows/docs-screenshots.yml Push to main (docs changed) Guide and API reference are built and published to GitHub Pages .github/workflows/docs.yml Release Release notes link the guide and the update notes; PRs labelled breaking-change appear under "Manual steps needed" .github/release-drafter.yml

docs.title: Documenting a new feature
docs.text:
1. Create the page in German, e.g. docs/user/funktionen/spenden.md, and its English translation spenden.en.md in the same folder. In the front matter of both, list the routes they describe:

    ---
routes:
  - /donations
---

# Donations

  2. Add it to the navigation in mkdocs.yml under nav: (German title), add the English title under nav_translations, and link it from funktionen/index.md and funktionen/index.en.md.

  3. Screenshot: add it to the SHOTS list in scripts/docs-screenshots/capture.mjs and embed it per language:

    ![Donations](../assets/screenshots/donations.png){ .screenshot }

    Both language versions reference the same donations.png; English pages are served donations.en.png automatically. The script finds buttons by their label in the app's translation files, so use t('…') with the i18n key instead of hard-coded text.

  4. Update affected pages: roles, overview, data protection, exporting your data.

  5. Does the update need manual steps from users? Then add an entry to the release notes in both languages using docs/templates/migration-guide.md, and label the PR breaking-change.

docs.title: Trying it locally
docs.text:
pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
npm run docs:serve        # preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000 (English at /en/)
npm run docs:build        # as in CI: coverage check + strict build
npm run docs:screenshots  # regenerate all screenshots (needs Go and Node)

docs:screenshots starts its own backend and frontend on ports 3101 and 5273 with a throwaway database, sets it up with demo data and captures every page, once per language. Your own installation is not touched. So that screenshots only change when the UI changes, the browser clock is frozen, animations are off, random IDs and timestamps in tables are replaced by fixed values, and a file is only overwritten if pixels changed beyond the colour tolerance for anti-aliasing. DOCS_LANGUAGES=en captures only one language.

docs.title: Writing style
docs.text:
• German: informal "du", short sentences, like in the app. English: plain, friendly, second person.
  • Write for volunteers without IT knowledge: what do I click, what happens then?
  • Put names of buttons and menus in bold, exactly as they appear in the app in that language.
  • Be honest: what doesn't work (yet) goes in a notice box.
  • No real personal data in examples or screenshots.

docs.title: Joining a club
docs.text: You were invited and received an invite code? Here's how to join.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Install Open ClubManager and create your account during first-run setup (option: "Together with others – I have an invite").
  • Accept the folder share you received from your club (Nextcloud, OneDrive, Dropbox, Google Drive …) and make sure the folder is synchronised to your computer.

docs.title: 1. Invite code
docs.text: Type or paste the 24-character code. Hyphens, spaces and upper/lower case don't matter. The code is valid for 7 days and works only once.

docs.title: 2. Storage location
docs.text:
Choose the shared folder. Open ClubManager shows which club is in it.

Existing data on this device

If there is already club data on your device, it is replaced by the club's data. A backup is saved next to the database beforehand automatically. You have to agree to this explicitly.

docs.title: 3. Your name
docs.text: Your name and the name of this device, so the others recognise you. Plus your password, which protects this device's key.

docs.title: 4. Safety code
docs.text:
You see a 6-digit safety code. Tell it to the person who invited you, ideally by phone. You only get access once they confirm it.

You can close Open ClubManager in the meantime. As soon as you are approved, you see "Welcome! You're in" and your role.

Wrong code or wrong folder? Cancel joining withdraws your request – on this screen or under Collaboration. You can try again right away.

Why a safety code?

The code makes sure that it really is you who used the invite, and not someone who intercepted the invite email.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text: Message What to do "We don't know this invite code" Check the code or ask for a new invite. If the invite was created just now, wait until your sync app has updated the folder and try again "There is no club in this folder" Check that you accepted the share and your sync app is running "The invite has expired / was already used" Ask for a new invite "This device was not admitted to the club" The board rejected the request. Contact them; "Try again" lets you join anew

docs.title: Setting up a club for collaboration
docs.text:
One board member does this, once. They get the role Board and can then invite the others.

Start via Collaboration → Turn on collaboration (or during first-run setup with "Together with others – set up a new club").

docs.title: 1. Storage location
docs.text:
Choose the shared folder. Open ClubManager lists Nextcloud, OneDrive, Dropbox and Google Drive folders it finds on your computer. Enter another folder … lets you enter your own path or a network drive (e.g. \\clubserver\board or /Volumes/Club).

Open ClubManager checks the folder:

  • is synchronised: fine
  • network drive: fine, if everyone can access it
  • doesn't seem to be synchronised: then others can't access the data
  • not writable or doesn't exist: check the path and your permissions

A subfolder "Open ClubManager – club name" is created in the folder.

docs.title: 2. Club and you
docs.text:
• Club name
  • Your name: how the others see you
  • Name of this device: e.g. "Laptop" or "Office PC"
  • Your password: the password you log in to Open ClubManager with. It protects this device's key.

The data already on this device becomes the club's starting state.

docs.title: 3. Emergency key
docs.text:
Open ClubManager generates an emergency key. Without it, nobody can get to the club data again if all board devices are lost.

  • Print it or save it as a file in a safe place, not in the shared folder.
  • As a check, you type the last 4 characters of the "check:" line.
  • After that step Open ClubManager does not keep the key.

More under Emergency key.

docs.title: 4. Done
docs.text: Next, invite the others.

docs.title: Collaboration
docs.text:
With collaboration, several board members work with the same club data, each on their own computer, even if you are not on the same network.

Still in development

Collaboration is new. Try it out, but only rely on it for real bank details once version 1.0 is released and the design has been reviewed by cryptography experts.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Chair's laptop            Treasurer's PC           Coach's laptop
 ┌──────────────┐          ┌──────────────┐          ┌──────────────┐
 │  own data    │          │  own data    │          │  own data    │
 └──────┬───────┘          └──────┬───────┘          └──────┬───────┘
        │      encrypted, signed changes                    │
        └───────────────►  shared folder  ◄─────────────────┘
               (Nextcloud, OneDrive, Dropbox, Google Drive, network drive)
  • Every device has its own database. You always work locally and fast, even without internet.
  • Changes are exchanged, not the database. Every change is encrypted, signed by the device and stored as a file in the shared folder. The other devices pick it up from there.
  • The folder only sees encrypted data. Neither your cloud provider nor anyone opening the folder can read member or bank data.
  • Permissions are enforced technically. A device with the coach role never receives the key for bank details, so it can't read them even if someone opens the files directly.
  • No server needed. You use a folder the club already has.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
1. A shared folder that everyone involved can write to and that is synchronised to their computers by the sync app of Nextcloud, OneDrive, Dropbox or Google Drive. A network drive works too if everyone can reach it (e.g. via VPN).
  2. Open ClubManager on every device.
  3. One board member who sets up the club and invites the others.

docs.title: Sync status
docs.text:
An icon in the header shows the state of collaboration:

Display Meaning Everything is in sync Your changes are in the folder, the others' changes have arrived. Synchronizing … Open ClubManager is exchanging changes (automatically every 30 seconds). Storage location not reachable The folder isn't available right now (e.g. offline). You can keep working; your changes wait and are transferred later. Please have a look There are conflicts to resolve, join requests or a problem. Waiting for your request to be approved You asked to join and the board still has to approve.

Synchronize now starts the exchange immediately.

How fast do changes arrive?

Open ClubManager itself checks every 30 seconds. How quickly a change reaches the others' folders depends on your cloud provider's sync app, usually seconds to a few minutes.

docs.title: Simultaneous changes
docs.text:
If two people change different fields of the same member at the same time (one the address, the other the IBAN), both changes are kept. If both change the same field, the later change wins.

Values that must be unique (membership numbers, email addresses, names of groups and sections) can end up assigned twice. This is shown under Needs attention.

docs.title: Pages in this section
docs.text:
• Set up a club
  • Join a club
  • Manage people & devices
  • Needs attention
  • Emergency key

docs.title: Needs attention
docs.text: Because every device also works offline, two people can assign the same unique value at the same time, for example both giving membership number 1042 to two different new members. Open ClubManager detects this and shows it under Collaboration → To resolve (also via the sync status "Please have a look").

docs.title: What can be duplicated?
docs.text:
• Membership numbers
  • Email addresses of members
  • Names of groups, roles and sections

docs.title: How to resolve it
docs.text:
For each case, Open ClubManager shows which entry keeps the value and which one must be changed. The rule: whoever assigned the value first keeps it.

Case Resolution Duplicate membership number Use the next free number or Choose a number Duplicate email address enter a new email address Duplicate name enter a new name

Click Apply. The change is distributed to everyone and the entry disappears from the list.

Anyone with write permission for the affected area can resolve it. Those who may only read see the notice but can't change anything.

docs.title: Emergency key
docs.text: The emergency key is generated once when you set up the club. With it, you regain access to your club data and administration when no device with the board role is available any more, for example because the only board laptop was stolen.

docs.title: Keeping it safe
docs.text:
• Keep it like a safe key: printed in the club's files, in a bank deposit box, at the chair's home.
  • Don't store it in the shared cloud folder: whoever has the folder and the emergency key has full access.
  • Nobody else can restore it, not even the Open ClubManager developers.

docs.title: Using it
docs.text:
Only use it when there really is no board device left.

  1. Install Open ClubManager on a device and start setup with Use the emergency key (or under Collaboration → Emergency).
  2. Paste or type the whole text of the emergency key. The lines club-id, root-sign-key, root-age-key and check are the important ones.
  3. Click Restore club.

This device is then a board device. Next, remove all lost devices under People & devices.

The emergency key stays valid; keep it safe again.

docs.title: Common errors
docs.text: Message Meaning "The emergency key is incomplete or contains a typo" check the text, especially the check line "This emergency key belongs to a different club" wrong key or wrong folder

docs.title: People & devices
docs.text: Under Collaboration you find the tabs Overview, People & devices, Invites, Roles and Emergency. Only the board may invite people, change roles and remove devices.

docs.title: Inviting a person
docs.text:
1. Who and which role: the person's name and their role (board, treasurer, secretary, coach, equipment manager). Open ClubManager shows what the role may do.
  2. Folder access: give the person write access to the shared folder at your cloud provider. This isn't done in Open ClubManager, but you get step-by-step instructions for Nextcloud, OneDrive, Dropbox or Google Drive.
  3. Invite code: send the person the code, e.g. by email or messenger. Show e-mail text gives you a ready-made text to copy.

The code is valid for 7 days and works once. Open invites are listed in the Invites tab, where you can withdraw them.

docs.title: Approving a join request
docs.text:
When the invited person joins, a join request appears for you.

  1. Call the person and ask for the safety code shown on their screen.
  2. Enter it and click Give access.

If the code doesn't match, reject the request: someone else used the invite. After three wrong codes, the request is rejected automatically.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
The five roles are fixed:

Role May Board see and edit everything, invite others Treasurer edit bank details and finances, see members and contacts Secretary maintain members and contact details Coach see the member list and inventory Equipment manager edit the inventory, see the member list

The full table is under Users & roles.

docs.title: Changing a role
docs.text: Under People & devices → Change role. If someone gets fewer permissions, they no longer see new data from the removed areas. What they have already seen stays on their device.

docs.title: Removing a device
docs.text:
If a device is lost or stolen, or someone leaves their position: People & devices → Remove device, and choose the reason.

Afterwards:

  • The device receives no new data.
  • Changes it makes from now on are ignored by everyone.
  • What is already stored on the device cannot be deleted.

Loss or theft: report the data breach

If a device with member data gets lost, this may be a data breach that must be reported to the data protection authority within 72 hours (Art. 33 GDPR). Disk encryption reduces the risk considerably.

You can't remove your own device. There must always be at least one device with the board role.
